reason: I'd type one sentence on a bad night after the kids are down, sure. But I paid for Calm and used it for three weeks, and I know exactly how that ends.
objection: I've been here before: I pay, I use it twice, it sits on my card for months.
would_change_my_mind: If it still had me using it after the free month without me forcing it, then maybe the yearly plan.

v1.why: A check-in sheet the second I sign in feels like homework, and the chat that isn't mine is confusing.

v2.why: Nicer start, but 'chapter 2 tomorrow' is just another thing I'll fall behind on.

v3.why: I like the optional journal and the words-not-scores, but I'd drift off it like everything else.

reason: I'll try it before a big meeting because it's free, but a computer writing a script about my anxiety feels off next to what I do with my therapist. And $10 a month is real money for me.
objection: An AI guessing at my feelings sounds generic at best and a little creepy at worst.
would_change_my_mind: If my therapist said it was fine to use between sessions, or if the first session actually sounded like it heard me.

v1.why: Percentages and up/down arrows on my wellness feel like being graded.

v2.why: Better that it's my own words, but still the same scores on progress.

v3.why: The 'Why?' on each change helps me trust it a bit, but not enough to make it part of my week.

reason: Free with a few sessions a day is more than I'd ever use, so why would I pay? YouTube has worked for me for years.
objection: It's another subscription I'd forget about, and the free part already covers me.

v1.why: Coins on every screen and a hamburger menu; it feels like a game wanting my money.

v2.why: Clean tabs and quick setup, I'd open it a few times and then go back to YouTube.

v3.why: More stuff (journal, wearables, reports) than I'm ever going to use.

reason: I'm up most weeknights scrolling anyway, so typing 'I can't switch off' into something is easy and I'd actually use it. But the free sessions cover a night or two a week, and $10 is too much on my budget on top of therapy.
objection: I pay for therapy already; another monthly charge I'll stop opening is the last thing I need.
would_change_my_mind: A cheaper plan around $4 or $5, or the free tier stopping right when it was working.

v1.why: An example conversation about someone else's REM score is not where I want to start at 1am.

v2.why: Starting from my own sentence and a chapter waiting tomorrow could get me off the scroll, on the free tier.

v3.why: Same as v2 and the progress in words feels less like a report card, still free tier though.

reason: I check my sleep score every morning and I try everything new, so a session built from how I said I felt is exactly my kind of experiment. If it reads my Oura I'd pay the $10 to see if the score moves.
objection: I don't want it pinging me with questions every day; I want it to read my ring, not interrogate me.

v1.why: A daily check-in sheet on sign-in is exactly the nagging I hate.

v2.why: Three skippable questions once is fine and the chapters are a nice hook.

v3.why: Wearable option off until I switch it on plus 'Why?' on changes is the version I'd tell people about.

reason: I'll try it the week it comes out, that's who I am. Whether I pay depends on whether the voice and script sound like a person or like a template, and my bet is template.
objection: AI-made meditation tends to sound flat and slightly uncanny, and I'm not paying to hear that.
would_change_my_mind: If the first two sessions genuinely sounded better than what I get free on Calm's free tier or YouTube.

v1.why: Feels like a demo, with someone else's chat in my screen.

v2.why: Better onboarding but the content is the question, not the menu.

v3.why: Wearable link and progress in words are good ideas, but I'd stop if the audio feels generic.

reason: I don't want an AI writing things for my head, especially about how I feel. Between work and the kids I'd rather put on a podcast I already trust.
objection: AI content about mental health, plus an app that keeps asking how I feel every day.
would_change_my_mind: A real clinician or person I trust standing behind what it says, and no daily questions.

v1.why: A daily check-in sheet the moment I sign in, no thanks.

v2.why: 'How do you feel now?' after every session is still the app asking me questions.

v3.why: At least it explains its suggestions and the journal is optional, but I still don't trust AI with this.

reason: Forty minutes with headphones each way, I could try a session on the train. But I already have free apps and YouTube queued up, and I cancelled Headspace for a reason.
objection: I already have free stuff for this that I don't use enough; paying didn't fix that last time.
would_change_my_mind: A proper phone app that works offline on the train, and a lower price.

v1.why: Coins and a check-in sheet up front, it's busy.

v2.why: Bottom tabs are easy on the train, but a browser app on a patchy signal won't last.

v3.why: Calmer feel, but I'd still default back to my podcasts.

reason: Before a bad meeting I might type one line and see what comes out, because it's free. I've never paid for one of these and a chat that wants to talk back isn't going to be the first.
objection: I don't want an app asking me questions every day; I want to press play and be done.

v1.why: Daily check-in sheet plus a chat full of someone else's sleep data, too much.

v2.why: Simplest of the three, but 'how do you feel now' after each one gets old fast.

v3.why: Journal, wearables, reports: more for me to ignore.

reason: Free is the only price I've ever paid for this kind of thing and a few sessions a day is plenty. $10 a month is a dinner out on my budget.
objection: Another subscription I'll sign up for and forget about.
would_change_my_mind: A student-style cheaper plan, under $5, after I'd already used it every week for a month.

v1.why: Feels cluttered with coins and percentages.

v2.why: Nice welcome, but I'd forget it in a week like my journal.

v3.why: The optional journal is tempting, but I never keep journals up either.
